proposed.text: Under the 2024 BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum height for edge protection curbs on accessible ramps, and what is the rationale for this requirement?

options.text: 50 mm minimum; to prevent water ingress into the ramp structure, which is not the primary concern for edge protection
75 mm minimum; to provide sufficient visual contrast between the ramp surface and the drop edge, enhancing safety for visually impaired users
100 mm minimum; to prevent wheelchair casters or crutch tips from slipping over the edge and causing falls
150 mm minimum; to meet the structural deflection requirements for cantilevered ramp edges, which is not typically a requirement for edge protection curbs

proposed.rationale: Section A.1.2.h of the 2024 IRR Appendix A requires minimum 100mm high curbs/raised edges on both sides of accessible ramps with open edges. The rationale is safety: wheelchair casters and crutch tips can slip over low edges, causing falls. This curb requirement operates alongside the 1,100mm minimum guard/railing height (per PD 1096 Rule XII) for ramps elevated more than 750mm above adjacent grade. The curb handles the lower-level fall prevention; the guardrail handles the higher-level protection.
